solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Explain illumination in hut

parts.note: a shed is a simple hut
light is illumination
on can mean in, as in 'on the team'

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks for illumination inside a garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are assembled in the order hut, illumination, in, not the order the clue gives them.
explanation.definitionFit: To clarify something is to make it plain, the idiom for explaining a matter.

clue.text: Theo had become an impetuous person

indicators.note: the letters of the two names-and-verb words become something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Theo has turned into someone rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' turns the seven letters of THEO HAD into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash, quick-tempered individual is called this, a common synonym.

clue.text: One trapped by shellfish during exploit made speech

indicators.note: during places the shellfish-and-one block inside the exploit word

parts.note: a deed is an exploit or feat

indicators.note: being trapped by the shellfish means the one sits inside it

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone caught by a clam mid-adventure gave a speech about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate or speak rhetorically in public; delivered a speech is the sense.

clue.text: Bring upon oneself without interest without debts

indicators.note: the second without asks for the debts word to be dropped from the first word

parts.note: lacking curiosity, uninterested
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Someone takes on obligations despite having no interest and no debts.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'without' tricks: the first is part of a definition (INCURIOUS), the second removes IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or penalty is to bring it upon oneself, a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Cambridge University

parts.note: not the English one: the famous university in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: It looks like a plain reference to the English university.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge, Massachusetts, near Boston, is home to Harvard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League institution sits in the American city of Cambridge, so the phrase literally describes it.

clue.text: Speech from Nelson not starting before noon

indicators.note: not starting means the admiral's first name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Horatio Nelson, the British admiral

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson's address that failed to begin before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio Nelson was Britain's great naval hero; 'not starting' drops the H from HORATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal public address is an oration, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bird's second present, flags

parts.note: now means the present time
bunting is a string of small flags

explanation.surface: A bird's second gift of flags.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Bird stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow bunting is a white-winged finch-like songbird of the Arctic.

clue.text: Vocal ructions start to echo in secluded place

indicators.note: ructions are uproar or disturbance, so the vocal letters are thrown about
start to means only the opening letter of the echo word

explanation.surface: Loud vocal rows start an echo in a quiet nook.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess or nook set back from a room is a secluded spot.

clue.text: Nothing to do with the ear or to do with the river

parts.note: nil means nothing
otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A choice between nothing to do with hearing or a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The river is the Nile, a crossword favourite for 'river'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic means relating to the Nile, the river of Egypt and Sudan.

clue.text: Pen Romeo found amongst colourful skeletons

indicators.note: found amongst places the Romeo letter inside the reef word

parts.note: coral is made of the skeletons of tiny sea creatures, often brightly coloured
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A writer's pen turns up among vivid bones.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure for livestock is a pen, the noun sense here.

clue.text: Ham starting developing into comedian's stooge

indicators.note: developing means the letters grow into a different form

explanation.surface: An over-acting ham begins turning into a comic's sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing into' rearranges HAM STARTING; 'into' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The partner who feeds lines to a comic in a double act is the foil or stooge.

clue.text: Military site warrant officer needs time to follow order

indicators.note: to follow puts the time word after the order

parts.note: WO is the military abbreviation for warrant officer
OM is the Order of Merit
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An officer needs time to obey a command at the base.
explanation.walkthrough: Woomera is a rocket-testing range in South Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Australian rocket range is a well-known defence testing ground.

clue.text: Person who is fancy-free?

parts.note: fancy-free normally means unattached; here it means free of fancies, sticking to facts

explanation.surface: It reads as asking for someone carefree and unattached.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatist who sees things as they are has no flights of imagination.

clue.text: Topple in a stupendous way

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the adjective that follows

explanation.surface: Knocking something over in spectacular fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn or tip over is to topple, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Academic came unstuck preceding very good turn in the country

indicators.note: preceding puts the rearranged block before the turned piece
coming unstuck means falling apart, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: a don is a university academic

indicators.note: turn means the very good letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, very good

explanation.surface: An academic fell apart before a fine performance abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came unstuck' mixes DON and CAME into MACEDON; A1 written as AI is turned to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia is the former name of the Balkan state now called North Macedonia.

clue.text: One is not employed to mind one's own business

definitions.text: One is not employed to mind one's own business

parts.words: One is not employed to mind one's own business
parts.note: mind one's own business usually means don't interfere; here it is literal: such a worker looks after someone else's premises

explanation.surface: Sounds like a rule about nosy workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor or custodian is paid to look after a building owned by somebody else.

clue.text: Hard task for steeplejack?

definitions.meaning: a request from a tall-structure climber would be an order for something lofty

explanation.surface: A tough job for someone who climbs church spires.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a demand that is hard to meet; a steeplejack's work order is literally high.

clue.text: Rather big hit smashed rig inside

indicators.note: inside places the rearranged rig letters within the hit word

parts.note: to lash is to hit

indicators.note: smashed means the rig letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sizeable blow that wrecked an oil rig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' reads as a noun for a success, but it is the verb meaning whip; 'smashed' signals the rearrangement and 'inside' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat large or fairly sizeable, the -ish suffix softening the size.

clue.text: Switch positions before emergency room in America becomes available

parts.note: a switch's two positions are on and off
ER is the American abbreviation for a hospital's emergency room

explanation.surface: Flicking switches ahead of an American hospital visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods being offered for sale are available to buyers, the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Brick unhesitatingly making ringing sound

indicators.note: unhesitatingly asks for the hesitation sound er to be removed

parts.note: a clanger, like a brick, is a blunder in British slang (dropping a brick or a clanger)

explanation.surface: A brick makes a ring without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping a brick' and 'dropping a clanger' are British idioms for a blunder; ER is the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud metallic resonance, like a bell or pan struck, is a clang.

clue.text: Mark almost going to doctor with nothing on in city

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed beneath, so the nothing letter goes last
almost means the last letter of the mark is dropped

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone nearly reaches the doctor while naked in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Colombo is the commercial capital of Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the largest city of Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Not caring about good behaviour in the morning examination

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Someone indifferent to manners at a morning exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Without moral sense, neither caring for nor against right conduct.

clue.text: Anxious, jittery over sun

indicators.note: jittery means shaky, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Worried and jumpy about the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jittery' looks like a second definition beside Anxious, but here it is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Worried or on edge, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Not much of a fight

explanation.surface: A minor skirmish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small bit of something and an informal fight.

clue.text: Resolve to reveal information back in the pavilion

parts.note: to talk is to blab or disclose secrets
in cricket a dismissed batsman, who is out, returns to the pavilion

explanation.surface: Deciding to spill secrets once back in the clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket pavilion is the clubhouse beside the field; a batsman who is out goes back there.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a disagreement by discussing it thoroughly is the idiom.

clue.text: Take a little from both ends of loaf in landing-place

indicators.note: in puts the loaf ends within the landing-place

parts.note: a pier is a landing-place for boats

indicators.note: both ends means the first and last letters of the bread word

explanation.surface: Stealing part of a loaf at the jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal small amounts, petty theft, is to take a little.

clue.text: One member in King's Arms initially before reaching the French capital!

indicators.note: in puts the one-and-member block between the two initials
initially means the first letters of the king and arms words

parts.note: A is one
MP is a Member of Parliament
la is the feminine French for the

explanation.surface: A member at a King's Arms pub before heading to the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Arms is a typical British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kampala is the capital city of Uganda.

clue.text: He must be Cain

parts.note: Cain was born after Adam and Eve, so third human; and he is the pronoun of that grammatical form

explanation.surface: Identifying a culprit as the Bible's first murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam and Eve came first, so Cain, their son, was the next human; 'he' is grammatically this too.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun 'he' belongs to the grammatical category used for someone spoken about.
